**Pathology Report**

---

**Specimen Identification:**  
Bronchoscopy – Transbronchial core needle biopsies, Left Lower Lobe (segmental bronchus)

**Date of Procedure:** *[date omitted]*  

**Type of Specimen:** Formalin‐fixed, paraffin‑embedded (FFPE) core biopsy material; 4 separate cores obtained.

---  

### GROSS DESCRIPTION  

Received in formalin were four cylindrical core fragments measuring **0.7 cm**, **0.6 cm**, **0.5 cm**, and **0.4 cm** in greatest dimension; collectively submitted in cassette #LUL‑TBX‑01. The specimens are tan-white, firm, and appear homogeneous without obvious necrosis or hemorrhage. Sections were taken uniformly throughout each core.

---  

### MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS  

Low power examination reveals diffuse infiltration of the alveolar septa and peribronchiolar interstitium by small to intermediate sized lymphocytes forming loosely cohesive nodules. Scattered plasma cell–like cells with eccentric nuclei and abundant basophilic cytoplasm are admixed. There is preservation of underlying architecture with occasional residual respiratory epithelium seen. Mitotic figures are rare (<1/10 HPF). No overt sheets of blasts, significant fibrosis, granulomas, or necrotizing vasculitis identified.

High power evaluation shows:

* Small mature lymphocytes possessing irregular nuclear contours, scant cytoplasm, and inconspicuous nucleoli.  
* Plasmacytoid differentiation evident in focal areas (cytoplasmic eosinophilia, “clockface” chromatin).  
* Occasional centroblast‑type cells absent; lack of follicle center pattern.  

Overall morphology is most compatible with an extranodal marginal zone B‑cell lymphoma (MALT‑type).

---  

### IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY / ANCILLARY STUDIES  

| Marker | Result | Interpretation |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| CD20   | Positive (strong membranous) | Confirms B‑cell lineage |
| PAX5   | Positive (moderate) | Supports B‑cell phenotype |
| CD79a  | Positive (diffuse) | B‑cell marker |
| BCL2   | Positive (uniform) | Anti‑apoptotic protein expression typical of marginal zone lymphoma |
| CD5    | Negative | Excludes mantle cell lymphoma & CLL/SLL |
| CD10   | Negative | Rules out germinal centre derived neoplasms (follicular lymphoma, Burkitt) |
| Cyclin D1 | Negative | Further excludes mantle cell lymphoma |
| Ki‑67 (MIB‑1) | Low proliferative index (~10%) | Consistent with indolent behavior |
| Light chain restriction (κ/λ ISH) | κ light chain restricted | Demonstrates clonality |

No evidence of EBV‑encoded RNA (EBER) positivity. Molecular testing for IGH rearrangement pending (not required for definitive diagnosis in this context).

---  

### DIAGNOSTIC CONCLUSION  

**Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (MALT-type) involving the left lower lobe bronchopulmonary parenchyma, WHO Grade 1.**  
Immunoprofile: CD20⁺, BCL2⁺, CD5⁻, CD10⁻, κ light‑chain restricted.  

These findings correlate with the previously established clinical staging of AJCC stage IA (T2 N0 M0) marginal zone lymphoma of the lung.

---  

**Prepared By:**  
Dr. ***[Name]***, MD  
Department of Anatomic Pathology  

**Verified By:** _______________________   (Signature)  

*(Report generated electronically; no handwritten signature attached.)*

**Next‑Generation Sequencing (NGS) Report – Comprehensive Genomic Profiling**

---

### Patient Information  
**Name:** Emily Chen  **Age/Sex:** 34/Female  

### Specimen Details  
| Item                     | Description                              |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Specimen Type**        | Formalin‑fixed paraffin‑embedded (FFPE) core needle biopsy of left lower‐lobe lung lesion |
| **Accession / Specimen ID** | LUNG‑MLZL‑0322‑01                         |
| **Date of Collection**   | *[date omitted]*                           |
| **Submitting Clinician** | Pulmonology Oncology Service               |

### Test Performed  
Comprehensive targeted DNA/RNA panel covering >400 genes implicated in hematologic malignancies, including detection of single nucleotide variants (SNVs), insertions/deletions (indels), copy number alterations (CNAs), structural rearrangements, and immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) V(D)J clonality.

#### Methodology Overview  
1. **DNA Extraction:** FFPE tumor material macrodissected (>30 % neoplastic cellularity). Quantified via Qubit dsDNA HS assay.  
2. **Library Preparation:** Hybrid capture using custom oncology probe set (Illumina TruSight™ Oncology 500 design). Unique Molecular Identifiers (UMIs) incorporated.  
3. **Sequencing Platform:** Illumina NovaSeq 6000, paired‑end 150 bp reads. Mean target depth ≈ 800×; ≥95 % bases covered at >200×.  
4. **Bioinformatic Pipeline:** Alignment to hg19 reference genome (BWA-MEM), variant calling (Mutect2/Strelka2), CNA determination (FACETS), IGH clonotype assembly (MiXCR). Variant annotation through COSMIC, ClinVar, OncoKB.  
5. **Quality Metrics:** All QC parameters met laboratory acceptance criteria (duplicate rate ≤15 %, uniformity ≥90 %). No evidence of sample contamination.

### Detected Genomic Alterations  

| Gene      | alteration                | Protein change          | Allele Frequency* | Classification |
|-----------|----------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| **NOTCH2**| c.718 C>T                  | p.Arg240\***            | 14 %              | Likely pathogenic (gain‑of‑function truncation typical of marginal‑zone lymphomas) |
| **KLF2**  | c.298 C>A                 | p.Gln100\***             | 12 %              | Likely pathogenic (loss‑of‑function mutation frequently observed in extranodal MZL) |
| **TNFAIP3**| Homozygous deletion       | —                       | —                 | Pathogenic (NF‑κB inhibitor loss, promotes constitutive signaling) |
| **CREBBP**| c.4930 G>A                | p.Arg1644His           | 7 %               | Variant of uncertain significance (VUS); occurs in some indolent B‑cell neoplasms |
| **EP300** | c.4874 C>T                | p.Arg1625Cys           | 6 %               | VUS; acetyltransferase domain involvement |
| **MDM2**  | Copy‑Number Gain (≈ 5 copies) | —                    | —                 | Potentially amplifying (may attenuate TP53 function) |
| **IGHA/B Clonotype**| Dominant IGH V(D)J rearrangement identified | - | 8 % (clonal read proportion) | Confirms presence of a monoclonal B‑cell population |

\*Allele frequencies represent percentage of mutant allele among uniquely mapped reads after UMI deduplication.

### Interpretation  

- The **NOTCH2 truncating mutation** and **KLF2 loss‑of‑function substitution** constitute hallmark genomic lesions seen in marginal‑zone lymphoma (especially extranodal/MALT subtypes). Both promote aberrant NOTCH signaling and dysregulated transcription factor networks contributing to lymphomagenesis.  
- **Bi‑allelic loss of TNFAIP3** removes a critical negative regulator of the canonical NF‑κB pathway, reinforcing survival signals characteristic of marginal‑zone histologies.  
- Co‑occurring **CREBBP** and **EP300** missense changes involve residues within the HAT domains; while classified presently as VUS, similar alterations have been linked to altered chromatin remodeling in various indolent B‑cell disorders. Their functional impact remains speculative without orthogonal assays.  
- An **MDM2 copy‑number gain** raises the possibility of compromised TP53-mediated apoptosis, although the overall mutational burden does not suggest overt TP53 dysfunction. This finding may acquire therapeutic relevance if agents targeting the MDM2–p53 axis become indicated.  
- Detection of a **dominant IGH V(D)J clone (8 %)** corroborates the diagnosis of a clonal B‑cell proliferation and aligns with the morphologic identification of marginal‑zone lymphoma. The relatively modest clonal fraction reflects admixture with normal respiratory parenchyma inherent to small biopsies.  

Overall, the molecular profile supports the pathologic classification of **pulmonary extranodal marginal‑zone lymphoma**, providing biologic insight into the mechanisms driving disease persistence. While several alterations (e.g., NOTCH2, KLF2, TNFAIP3 loss) are considered “driver” events in this entity, none currently meet strict FDA‑approved biomarker thresholds for mandated targeted therapies. Nonetheless, awareness of these abnormalities may influence selection of investigational agents or enrollment in genotype‑matched trials (e.g., Notch pathway modulators, selective NF‑κB inhibition).

### Limitations  

- Testing performed on a limited-volume FFPE core; very low‑frequency subclones (<5 %) may escape detection.  
- RNA fusion partners were not assessed; however, fusions are uncommon in marginal‑zone lymphoma.  
- Functional consequences of the identified VUS cannot be definitively determined without complementary protein expression data.

### References (selected)

1. Raderer M et al. Genetic landscape of marginal zone lymphoma. *Blood*. 2019;133(24):2582‑2595.  
2. Swerdlow SH et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Ed. IARC Press, 2022.  
3. Oki Y et al. Role of NOTCH2 and KLF2 mutations in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma. *Leukemia*. 2021;35(4):1021‑1030.

**Chest Computed Tomography Report**

**Patient:** Emily Chen  
**Age:** 41 years  
**Sex:** Female  

---

### Examination Details
- **Study Type:** Multidetector computed tomography (CT) of the thorax, axial acquisition with multiplanar reconstructions.  
- **Technique:** Non‑contrast images obtained followed by intravenous administration of iodinated contrast (120 mL Iohexol, rate 3 mL/s). Images acquired from lung apices through adrenal glands (~30 cm coverage) with ≤1 mm collimation, reconstructed in soft‐tissue and lung windows. No motion artifacts identified.  

---

### Findings  

#### Lungs & Airway
- **Left Lower Lobe:** Previously characterized solitary peripheral nodule measuring *approximately 2.2 cm* in maximal transverse dimension (previous measurement 3.0 cm on CT dated Age 39). The lesion demonstrates smooth margins, homogeneous attenuation, and minimal internal vascularity. There is no associated cavitation, calcification, or solid component change. Density measurements show mean Hounsfield units ≈ +25 HU on non‑contrast series, compatible with persistent low‑density lymphomatous tissue rather than fibrosis or necrosis. No new ground‑glass opacities, consolidations, or interstitial infiltrates are seen throughout both lungs.
- **Remaining Pulmonary Parenchyma:** Unremarkable. No additional focal lesions, atelectasis, or emphysematous changes. Scattered subsegmental bronchovascular markings within normal limits.

#### Mediastinum & Central Structures
- **Trachea / Main Bronchi:** Patent without wall thickening.
- **Carina & Segmental Airways:** Normal caliber.
- **Mediastinal/Hilar Nodes:** No enlargement. Short axis of largest node measures 7 mm (subcarinal region). All nodes remain below the typical threshold for pathological significance (<1 cm short axis). No evidence of necrotic centers.
- **Vascular Structures:** Thoracic aorta and great vessels demonstrate expected calibers and course. No aneurysm or dissection.

#### Pleura
- Bilateral visceral and parietal pleural surfaces appear intact. No effusion, pneumothorax, or pleural-based masses detected.

#### Upper Abdomen (included portion)
- Visualized portions of liver, spleen, adrenals, and kidneys exhibit normal morphology and attenuation. No focal hepatic lesions or splenic abnormalities.

#### Osseous Structures
- Visible ribs, vertebral bodies, and scapulae display preserved trabecular pattern without destructive lesions or periosteal reaction.

---

### Comparison
- Compared with prior CT of the chest performed at age 39 (nodule 3.0 cm, low FDG avidity on preceding PET–CT), there is measurable decrease in the longest diameter of the left lower lobe nodule to 2.2 cm, indicating interval regression.

---

### Impression
1. **Interval reduction** of the known left lower lobe marginal zone lymphoma (extranodal/MALT) nodule from 3.0 cm to 2.2 cm, suggestive of favorable therapeutic response to ongoing ibrutinib therapy.  
2. No new intrathoracic lymphadenopathy, pleural involvement, or secondary pulmonary lesions identified.  
3. Overall thoracic structures unremarkable aside from above finding.

At age 32, the patient was diagnosed with marginal zone lymphoma, extranodal (MALT) of the lung, AJCC stage I (T2 N0 M0), Summary Stage I, Histology: MARGINAL ZONE LYMPHOMA, EXTRANODAL (ICD‑O‑3 9689/3), asymptomatic, ECOG 0.
At age 32, bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy confirmed marginal zone lymphoma, CD20+, BCL2+, CD5‑, CD10‑.
At age 32, NGS of lung tissue revealed NOTCH2 p.R240*, KLF2 p.Q100*, TNFAIP3 loss, and additional alterations: CREBBP p.R1644H, EP300 p.R1625C, and a copy‑number gain of 12q13 (MDM2). A dominant IgH/V(D)J clonal sequence was present at 8% frequency.
At age 32, the oncologist documented active pulmonary marginal zone lymphoma; disease was present but non‑symptomatic.
At age 32, a chest CT showed a 2.5 cm left lower lobe nodule with mild enhancement; cancer was present and stable.
At age 33, the patient began rituximab 375 mg/m² every 8 weeks for six doses.
At age 33, after three rituximab infusions, the patient’s cough improved; disease was responding.
At age 33, the patient experienced a grade 2 infusion reaction (urticaria) during the fourth rituximab infusion, treated with antihistamines.
At age 34, PET‑CT demonstrated decreased metabolic activity of the lung nodule (SUVmax 2.1 vs 5.6 baseline); disease was responding.
At age 34, the patient reported being 8 weeks pregnant (confirmed by ultrasound).
At age 34, the patient was advised to hold further rituximab due to pregnancy; no additional systemic therapy was given.
At age 35, the patient’s pregnancy progressed uneventfully; lymphoma remained stable on imaging.
At age 36, a low‑dose chest CT performed for obstetric monitoring showed unchanged lung nodule size; disease was stable.
At age 37, after delivery, the patient elected to observe; no further therapy was administered.
At age 38, the patient developed postpartum hypertension (grade 1), managed with lifestyle modifications.
At age 39, routine follow‑up imaging showed mild increase in nodule size to 3.0 cm with unchanged low FDG uptake; disease was stable.
At age 40, the patient initiated ibrutinib 560 mg daily as delayed therapy.
At age 40, after three months of ibrutinib, the patient noted improved energy; disease was responding.
At age 41, CT chest demonstrated reduction of the lung nodule to 2.2 cm; cancer was responding.
At age 41, the patient experienced grade 1 diarrhea, attributed to ibrutinib, managed with loperamide.

**Pathology Report**

---

### Patient  
Name: **Anna Schmidt** Age: **57 years** Sex: Female  

### Specimen Identification  
*Specimen ID:* **BM‑057‑A**  
*Accession #:* 2025‑001234  
*Site of Biopsy:* Posterior Superior Iliac Spine – Bone Marrow Core Biopsy  

### Date of Procedure  
[Date omitted per instruction]  

### Type of Specimen  
Bone‑marrow core biopsy (multiple cores, total length ≈ 2 cm)

---  

## GROSS DESCRIPTION  
Three contiguous core segments measuring 0.7 cm, 0.8 cm, and 0.9 cm in length respectively (total aggregate length ≈ 2 cm) were submitted in formalin. The specimens appear tan‑pink, firm, and trabeculated. No obvious hemorrhage or necrosis observed macroscopically. All material processed routinely and embedded in paraffin.

---  

## MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION  

**Histologic Architecture:**  
Sections reveal markedly hypercellular marrow (>80 % cellularity) largely replaced by sheets of abnormal plasma cells. Normal hematopoietic elements are markedly reduced. Scattered normal fat spaces remain.

**Plasma Cell Morphology:**  
Neoplastic plasma cells display eccentric nuclei with coarse “clock‑face” chromatin, occasional nucleoli, and moderate anisokaryosis. Cytoplasm is abundant, basophilic, frequently containing prominent Golgi zones (“perinuclear hof”). Occasional binucleation and plasmablastic morphology (high nuclear/cytoplasmic ratios, prominent nucleoli) are seen (<10 %). Mitotic figures are rare.

**Extent of Infiltration:**  
Clonally infiltrating plasma cells constitute approximately **48 %** of the evaluated marrow area (estimated by visual quantitation across multiple fields).

---  

## IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY / FLOW CYTOMETRY  

| Marker | Result |
|--------|--------|
| **CD138 (Syndecan‑1)** | Strong membranous positivity in ≥95 % of neoplastic cells |
| **CD56 (NCAM)** | Positive (diffuse) |
| **CD20** | Negative |
| **kappa Light Chain** | Restrictive expression (positive) |
| **lambda Light Chain** | Absent |
| **Cyclin D1** | Negative |
| **Ki‑67 (MIB‑1)** | Low proliferative index (~5–8 %) |

Flow cytometric analysis corroborates the IHC profile: CD138+/CD38+ population comprising ~50 % of gated viable cells, expressing surface CD56, lacking CD19/CD20, demonstrating intracellular κ-restriction with λ-negative staining.

---  

## ANCILLARY STUDIES  

- **Cytogenetic Evaluation (Conventional Karyotype):** Not performed on this specimen.  
- **Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH):** Pending; ordered to assess for recurrent MM-associated aberrancies (e.g., t(14;16)/IGH‑MAF, 1q21 gain, del(13q)). Results unavailable at time of reporting.  
- **Next‑Generation Sequencing (NGS):** Not requested for this initial diagnostic sample.

---  

## DIAGNOSTIC CONCLUSION  

1. **Multiple Myeloma**, IgA κ paraproteinemia — bone‑marrow involvement estimated at **≈48 %** clonal plasma cell infiltration.  
   - Phenotypic profile: CD138+, CD56+, CD20‑, κ light‑chain restricted.  
2. Adequate tissue submitted for forthcoming molecular cytogenetic studies (FISH/NGS) to refine risk stratification.

No additional comments regarding therapeutic options are provided herein, as per standard pathology reporting practice.

**Imaging Report – Whole‑Body Positron Emission Tomography / Computed Tomography (PET‑CT)**  

---

### Patient Information  
- **Name:** Anna Schmidt  
- **Age/Gender:** 57‑year‑old Female  

### Study Details  
- **Modality:** Integrated ^18F‑FDG PET combined with low‑dose CT (whole‑body).  
- **Indication:** Staging/evaluation of multiple myeloma following initial diagnosis (stage III ISS). Baseline comparison requested to assess therapeutic response.  
- **Technique Summary:** After fasting ≥ 6 hours, blood glucose measured at 92 mg/dL. Intravenous injection of 370 MBq (≈10 mCi) ^18F‑fluorodeoxyglucose administered. Uptake period of 60 minutes before acquisition. Low‑dose helical CT performed for attenuation correction and anatomical correlation (120 kVp, automated mA modulation). Images reconstructed in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes; maximum intensity projection (MIP) generated.   

--- 

## FINDINGS  

| Region | Lesion(s) Identified | Size (largest dimension) | Morphology & Location | FDG Activity (SUVmax) |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| **Skull** | Multiple osteolytic foci involving calvarium (parietal and occipital bones) | 0.8–1.2 cm | Well‑defined lucent defects without cortical expansion | 3.9–4.7 |
| **Spine** | Scattered vertebral body involvement (T7, T10, L2) | ≤ 0.9 cm | Small focal lysis, mild endplate irregularity | 3.5–4.2 |
| **Pelvis** | Two lytic lesions: sacral ala (right) and left ilium near acetabulum | 1.4 cm (sacrum), 1.1 cm (ilium) | Cortical breach with adjacent soft‑tissue component minimal | 4.3 (sacrum), 4.0 (ilium) |
| **Ribs** | Several subcentimeter punctate erosions bilaterally | ≤ 0.7 cm | No associated mass effect | 3.2–3.8 |
| **Long Bones** | No additional osseous abnormalities identified in femora, tibiae, humeri. | — | — | — |
| **Extramedullary Soft Tissue** | Single nodule in the left posterior thigh, deep to the musculature of the hamstring compartment | 1.5 cm × 1.2 cm × 0.9 cm | Homogeneous density on CT, mildly enhancing post‑contrast reference series (if available); situated intramuscularly without obvious neurovascular encroachment. | 5.1 |
| **Viscera (Thoracic/Abdominal Organs)** | No abnormal FDG avidity in liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, kidneys, bowel, or lymph nodes exceeding physiologic background. | — | — | — |

*Background hepatic and splenic uptake normal (hepatic SUVmean ≈ 2.5). No evidence of diffuse marrow hypermetabolism beyond expected pattern for treated myeloma.*

### Additional Observations  
- No pleural effusion, ascites, or suspicious pulmonary nodules detected.  
- Cardiothoracic structures unremarkable; mediastinal vascular caliber within limits.  
- Musculoskeletal alignment preserved; no acute fractures seen.  

--- 

## IMPRESSION  

1. **Multiple Myeloma – Osseous Disease**  
   - Persistent FDG‑avid lytic lesions in the skull, spine, ribs, and pelvis demonstrating modest metabolic activity (SUVmax 3.2–4.7).  
   - Compared with baseline examination (performed X months earlier), size and metabolic intensity of individual lesions remain essentially unchanged. This suggests *stable disease* rather than clear response or progression according to standard response criteria (e.g., International Myeloma Working Group PET response classification).

2. **Extramedullary Deposit**  
   - A solitary 1.5 cm intramuscular soft‑tissue focus in the left posterior thigh shows moderate FDG uptake (SUVmax 5.1). Appearance has not appreciably altered relative to prior imaging; therefore, regarded as *stable* extramedullary involvement.

3. **Absence of New Sites**  
   - No newly emergent skeletal or visceral lesions identified. No evidence of transformation or aggressive disease behavior.

Overall, the whole‑body PET‑CT demonstrates **stable metabolically active disease** with both medullary and limited extramedullary components, correlating clinically with “neither responding nor progressing” status at this juncture. Continued surveillance with periodic functional imaging recommended per treating hematology team’s protocol.

**Oncology Consultation Note – Initial Visit**

---

### Patient Information  
- **Name:** Anna Schmidt  
- **Age:** 57 years  
- **Sex:** Female  

---  

## CHIEF COMPLAINT  
Evaluation of newly diagnosed multiple myeloma with evidence of end‑organ damage (CRAB).

---  

## HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS  
Anna Schmidt is a 57‑year‑old woman who presented three weeks ago with worsening fatigue, intermittent low‑grade fevers, and diffuse bone pain involving the lumbar spine and pelvic girdle. Laboratory workup performed at an outside facility revealed a monoclonal spike (IgA kappa) and mild hypercalcemia. She subsequently underwent a comprehensive hematologic work‑up:

* Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP): M‑protein 1.2 g/dL (IgA λ negative, IgA κ positive).  
* Urine immunofixation: Bence–Jones proteinuria ≈ 400 mg/24 h.  
* Free light chains: κ 250 mg/L, λ 1250 mg/L → κ/λ ratio ≈ 0.2.  
* CBC: Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL (normocytic, normochromic), WBC 5.9 × 10^9/L, platelets 210 × 10^9/L.  
* Comprehensive metabolic panel: Calcium 11.4 mg/dL (reference 8.5‑10.2 mg/dL), albumin 3.7 g/dL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL (eGFR ≈ 68 mL/min/1.73 m²).  

Bone‑marrow aspirate/biopsy performed at our institution confirmed a clonal plasma cell infiltrate comprising 48 % of nucleated cellularity. Immunophenotype: CD138+, CD56+, CD20−, cytoplasmic κ light‑chain restricted. Cytogenetics/FISH identified standard‐risk abnormalities without detectable del(17p) or t(4;14). Whole‑body ^18FDG PET‑CT disclosed multiple osteolytic foci in the calvarium and pelvis plus a solitary 1.5 cm subcutaneous nodule in the posterolateral aspect of the left thigh, demonstrating moderate FDG uptake (SUVmax 4.2). No overt organomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

Given the constellation of hypercalcemia, anemia, and radiographically evident bone destruction, she satisfies “active” disease per International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) criteria (CRAB). There is currently no indication of renal insufficiency attributable to cast nephropathy, though borderline eGFR warrants observation.

She denies recent infections, weight loss (>5 kg), night sweats, or neurologic deficits. No prior chemotherapy, radiation, or stem‑cell transplantation. 

---  

## REVIEW OF SYSTEMS  
| System | Positive / Negative |
|--------|---------------------|
| Constitutional | Fatigue (+), low‑grade fever (+), unintentional weight change (none) |
| HEENT | Headache (absent), visual changes (absent) |
| Cardiovascular | Chest discomfort (absent), palpitations (absent) |
| Respiratory | Dyspnea on exertion (mild), cough (none) |
| Gastrointestinal | Anorexia (moderate), nausea/vomiting (none), constipation (none) |
| Genitourinary | Polyuria/polydipsia (present, attributed to hypercalcemia) |
| Musculoskeletal | Bone pain (lumbar & pelvic, +), fractures (no reported) |
| Neurologic | Peripheral neuropathy (absent) |
| Dermatologic | Skin rash (absent) |
| Psychiatric | Anxiety/depression (denied) |

---  

## PAST MEDICAL HISTORY  
- Hypertension, controlled with lisinopril 10 mg daily (diagnosed 2018).  
- Osteoarthritis of knees (acetaminophen PRN).  
- No prior malignancies.  

## SOCIAL HISTORY  
- Married, lives with husband; employed full‑time as elementary school teacher.  
- Never smoker; occasional wine (~1 glass/week).  
- No illicit drug use.  
- Exercise: walks 30 min most days.  

## FAMILY HISTORY  
- Mother alive, age 84, hypertension, breast cancer treated surgically at 66 (remission).  
- Father deceased (stroke, age 72).  
- One sibling healthy.  

## ALLERGIES  
- NKDA (No Known Drug Allergies).  

## CURRENT MEDICATIONS  
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO QD  
- Acetaminophen 500 mg PO q6h prn joint pain  
- Multivitamin daily  

---  

## PHYSICAL EXAMINATION  
**General:** Alert, oriented ×3, appears mildly fatigued, NAD.  
**Vital Signs:** BP 128/78 mmHg, HR 76 bpm, RR 14/min, Temp 36.8°C, SpO₂ 98 % RA.  
**HEENT:** Normocephalic, scleral icterus absent, oral mucosa moist.  
**Neck:** Supple, no cervical adenopathy.  
**Cardiac:** RRR, S1/S2 normal, no murmurs/rubs.  
**Respiratory:** Clear bilaterally, vesicular breath sounds, no wheezes.  
**Abdominal:** Soft, non‑distended, mild epigastric tenderness, liver span 12 cm, spleen not palpable.  
**Extremities:** No edema. Tenderness over lumbar paraspinals and bilateral hips. No obvious deformities. Subtle firm nodular area palpated deep to skin of left posterior thigh correlating with PET finding.  
**Neurological:** Strength 5/5 UE/LE, sensation intact, reflexes symmetric, gait steady.  

---  

## LABORATORY RESULTS (most recent)  
| Test | Result | Reference |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Hb | 10.8 g/dL | 12‑15 |
| Hct | 33 % | 36‑46 |
| WBC | 5.9 × 10^9/L | 4‑11 |
| Platelet | 210 × 10^9/L | 150‑450 |
| Ca total | 11.4 mg/dL | 8.5‑10.2 |
| Albumin | 3.7 g/dL | 3.5‑5.0 |
| Creatinine | 1.1 mg/dL | ≤1.0 (female) |
| eGFR | 68 mL/min/1.73 m² | ≥90 |
| β2‑microglobulin | 3.2 mg/L | 0‑2.5 (high) |
| LDH | 190 U/L | 100‑220 |
| SPEP – M‑protein | 1.2 g/dL (IgA κ) | — |
| FLC κ | 250 mg/L | 3.3‑19.4 |
| FLC λ | 1250 mg/L | 5.7‑26.3 |
| κ/λ Ratio | 0.20 | 0.26‑1.65 |
| Hepatitis serologies | HBsAg neg, Anti‑HBc neg, HCV RNA pending (ordered) | — |

---  

## IMAGING FINDINGS  
**Whole‑Body ^18F‑FDG PET‑CT (performed 5 days ago)**  
- **Skull:** Multiple punctate lytic lesions throughout calvarial vault; modest FDG avidity (SUVmax 3.8).  
- **Pelvis:** Mixed sclerotic/lytic lesions in sacrum and both ilia; largest focus in right iliac wing measuring 1.2 cm, SUVmax 4.5.  
- **Spine:** Thoracic vertebrae demonstrate focal lucencies at T8/T9 without significant uptake.  
- **Soft tissue:** A 1.5 cm enhancing nodule in the left posterior proximal thigh, subfascial location, SUVmax 4.2—consistent with extramedullary plasmacytoma.  
- No mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy, hepatic/splenic involvement, or visceral masses.  

---  

## ASSESSMENT  
1. **Multiple Myeloma, Stage III (International Staging System)** – Confirmed IgA κ secretory disease with 48 % BM plasma cells, high-risk cytogenetic profile (pending FISH for del(17p)/t(4;14)), and active CRAB manifestations (hypercalcemia, anemia, extensive skeletal disease). Disease presently measurable (M‑protein 1.2 g/dL).  
2. **Hypercalcemia secondary to myelomatous bone resorption**, asymptomatic aside from polyuria/polydipsia.  
3. **Hypertension**, well controlled on ACE inhibition.  
4. **Potential HCV exposure** – testing ordered; result pending.  

---  

## PLAN  
1. **Management of Hypercalcemia**
   - Initiate aggressive hydration with isotonic saline 200 ml/hr aiming for urinary output >100 ml/hr; reassess electrolytes q6h.  
   - Add zoledronic acid 4 mg IV once (adjust dose for CrCl >50 mL/min) to inhibit osteoclastic activity; schedule subsequent dosing every 4 weeks contingent on renal function.  
   - Monitor corrected calcium q12h until ≤10.5 mg/dL, then transition to maintenance oral calcitonin if needed.  

2. **Induction Therapy**
   - Begin triplet regimen **bortez (Velcade®) 1.3 mg/m² SC weekly Days 1, 8, 15, 22**, **Lenalidomide (Revlimid™) 25 mg PO nightly Days 1‑21**, and **Dexamethasone 40 mg PO weekly** (standard VRd protocol).  
   - Counsel regarding prophylactic anticoagulation (apixaban 2.5 mg BID) owing to lenalidomide‑associated VTE risk, unless contraindicated.  
   - Prescribe acyclovir 400 mg PO BID for herpes zoster prophylaxis throughout PI exposure.  

3. **Supportive Care**
   - Continue lisinopril; hold if acute kidney injury develops.  
   - Start vitamin D supplementation (cholecalciferol 800 IU daily) post‑hydration phase.  
   - Baseline audiometry before initiating Velcade (potential ototoxicity).  
   - Discuss fertility preservation (not applicable; patient completed childbearing).  

4. **Baseline Evaluations Prior to Chemotherapy**
   - Repeat CMP, CBC with differential, coagulation panel, quantitative immunoglobulins.  
   - Obtain formal cardiology clearance (ECG, transthoracic echo) given planned anthracycline‑free regimen but potential cumulative cardio‑toxicity from dexamethasone.  
   - Perform infectious disease consultation for HCV when PCR returns; defer anti‑CD38 agents until viral load cleared.  

5. **Monitoring Schedule**
   - Clinic visits biweekly for the first two cycles: assess symptom control, laboratory trends, toxicities (especially neuro‑sensory symptoms, cytopenias).  
   - Reassess disease markers (serum/urine M‑protein, free light chains) after Cycle 2 to gauge depth of response.  
   - Follow up PET‑CT after completion of four cycles to evaluate metabolic remission of existing lesions.  

6. **Patient Education & Consent**
   - Reviewed nature of multiple myeloma, goals of therapy (induce VGPR or better, prevent complications).  
   - Discussed side effect profiles of Velcade (peripheral neuropathy, thrombocytopenia), lenalidomide (myelosuppression, teratogenicity), and steroids (glucose elevation, mood swings).  
   - Provided printed material on managing hypercalcemia at home and signs warranting urgent attention (severe weakness, arrhythmia, confusion).  

7. **Follow‑Up Appointments**
   - Return to clinic in 7 days for hydration check and calcium trend.  
   - Oncology follow‑up scheduled for Day 14 to initiate first doses of VRd.  
   - Infectious disease appointment pending HCV PCR results (anticipated within next week).  

**Signature:** Dr. Michael Bauer, MD  
Medical Oncologist – Hematologic Malignancies

**Oncology Progress Note**

**Patient:** Anna Schmidt  
**Age/Sex:** 59‑year‑old Female (currently 58 y/o at time of encounter)  
**MRN:** [Redacted]  

---

### Chief Complaint
Routine follow‑up evaluation after completion of six cycles of frontline induction therapy (bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone).

--- 

### History of Present Illness  
Anna Schmidt was diagnosed with International Staging System (ISS) Stage III IgA‑kappa multiple myeloma 12 months ago (age 57). Initial work‑up demonstrated:

* Serum M‑protein 1.2 g/dL, urinary M‐spike 400 mg/24 h  
* Involved free light chain (κ) 250 mg/L, κ/λ ratio 0.2  
* Bone‑marrow involvement 48 % clonal plasma cells (CD138⁺, CD56⁺, CD20⁻, κ restricted)  
* Lytic osseous lesions involving skull & pelvis plus a 1.5 cm extramedullary deposit in the left posterior thigh  
* Hypercalcemia 11.4 mg/dL (CRAB feature)

She commenced frontline “VRd” (weekly subcutaneous bortezomib 1.3 mg/m², oral lenalidomide 25 mg days 1–21, dexamethasone 40 mg weekly) administered in 28‑day cycles. She tolerated the regimen reasonably well, reporting occasional Grade 1 fatigue and transient nausea managed with ondansetron PRN. No significant peripheral neuropathy was reported until Cycle 5 when she noted intermittent tingling in both feet—graded as ≤Grade 1.

After completing **six cycles**, laboratory reassessment shows:

| Test | Baseline | Current |
|------|----------|---------|
| Serum IgA M‑protein | 1.2 g/dL | 0.6 g/dL |
| Urine M‑protein (24 h) | 400 mg | 180 mg |
| Free κ Light Chain | 250 mg/L | 140 mg/L |
| κ/λ Ratio | 0.2 | 0.35 |
| Calcium (serum) | 11.4 mg/dL | 9.8 mg/dL (norm) |
| Hemoglobin | 10.7 g/dL | 11.4 g/dL |
| Platelet Count | 210 ×10⁹/L | 185 ×10⁹/L |
| Creatinine (eGFR) | 78 mL/min/1.73 m² | 80 mL/min/1.73 m² |

### TECHNIQUE
Whole‑body ^18F‑fluorodeoxyglucose (^18F‑FDG) PET performed following standard fasting (>6 hours). Blood glucose level measured at 92 mg/dL prior to injection. Approximately **370 MBq (10 mCi)** of ^18F‑FDG administered intravenously. Uptake phase lasted **≈60 minutes** before acquisition. Low‑dose non‑contrast CT obtained for attenuation correction and anatomical correlation (120 kVp, automated mA modulation, slice thickness 3 mm). Images reconstructed using OSEM algorithm with point spread function modeling. Correlative axial, coronal, and sagittal fused images reviewed. Prior PET/CT performed approximately 12 months ago used for comparative evaluation.

|----------|-------|------------|----------------------|

- **Mediastinum/Hilum:** Normal size lymph nodes (<1 cm short axis) with physiologic FDG distribution (SUV_max ≤ 2.0).

Diffuse skeletal marrow demonstrates mildly increased FDG activity relative to hepatic background (average SUV_mean ≈ 2.5), consistent with known systemic involvement rather than acute transformation. No focal “flare” phenomenon appreciated.

- **Airways/Bowel:** Unremarkable.  
- **Skin/Subcutis:** Apart from the left posterior thigh implant, no cutaneous FDG‑avid lesions.

### IMPRESSION
1. **Stable metabolic activity** in all previously documented multiple myeloma sites (skull, pelvic bones, left posterior thigh soft‑tissue deposit). No appreciable rise in SUV_max compared with the most recent prior PET/CT.  
2. **Absence of new FDG‑avid lesions** elsewhere in the body, suggesting no overt disease dissemination at this time.

## History of Present Illness  
Ms Schmidt returns for scheduled evaluation of her relapsed/refractory IgA kappa multiple myeloma. At age 57 she presented with ISS Stage III disease, hypercalcemia (Ca 11.4 mg/dL) and several osteolytic sites (skull, pelvis, left posterior thigh). Initial induction with **VRd** produced a VGPR (M‑protein ↓ to 0.6 g/dL). Subsequent lines included **DVd**, achieving a PR (M‑protein 0.3 g/dL), followed by pomalidomide–dex when anti‑CD38 therapy was withheld owing to active hepatitis C infection. After successful eradication of HCV with a direct‑acting antiviral course, Ms Schmidt enrolled in a phase I/II trial of a bispecific anti‑BCMA antibody administered per protocol (dose Q2 weeks). She tolerates the agent well, having experienced only a Grade 1 infusion‑related reaction managed with diphenhydramine pretreatment.

Over the last six months her serologic marker has remained modestly elevated (most recent SPEP M‑protein ≈ 0.45 g/dL) without appreciable trend upward or downward—consistent with *stable measurable disease*. Platelet counts, which were suppressed to ≤45 × 10^9/L during early PI‐containing regimens, have fully rebounded (>150 × 10^9/L) over the preceding three months. No new constitutional symptoms, bone pain, or neurologic deficits reported. She continues to express interest in enrolling in additional investigational programs contingent upon meeting hematologic safety thresholds.

## Assessment  

1. **IgA κ Multiple Myeloma – Relapsed/Refractory, Measurable Disease**  
   - Current serologic markers indicate stable disease (M‑protein ≈ 0.45 g/dL, slight rise in κ/λ ratio but clinically insignificant).  
   - Prior exposures: Proteasome inhibitors (bortez), immunomodulatory agents (lenalidomide, pomalidomide), anti‑CD38 monoclonal antibody (dara), bispecific anti‑BCMA (ongoing). Meets “triple‑class” definition.  

2. **Platelet Recovery**  
   - Counts sustained >150 × 10^9/L for >4 weeks; resolves previous grade 3 thrombocytopenia constraint.  

3. **Chronic Hepatitis C – Resolved**  
   - Completed DAA regimen; SVR confirmed. No longer a barrier to trial participation.  

4. **Peripheral Neuropathy – Grade 2**  
   - Likely sequela of cumulative bortez exposure; presently manageable, does not limit daily activities.  

5. **Trial Eligibility Consideration**  
   - With hematologic parameters restored (ANC ≥ 1.0 × 10^9/L, platelets ≥ 100 × 10^9/L) and viral remission, Ms Schmidt satisfies most inclusion criteria for emerging cellular or novel antigen‑targeted protocols (CAR‑T, next‑generation bispecifics). Ongoing surveillance recommended.

| **Laboratory Surveillance** | CBC, chemistry panel, quantitative immunoglobulin, and free light chains every 28 days. Promptly assess any drop in platelets or neutrophils. |
| **Imaging Follow‑Up** | Schedule repeat PET‑CT in 3 months to confirm continued stability; consider targeted MRI if symptomatic osseous site emerges. |
| **Peripheral Neuropathy Management** | Maintain gabapentin 300 mg TID as needed; encourage balance exercises; avoid re‑introduction of proteasome inhibitors unless absolutely necessary. |
| **Clinical Trial Screening** | Coordinate with research office to initiate eligibility work‑up for a Phase II BCMA‑directed CAR‑T product (requires leukapheresis). Ensure collection window aligns with adequate blood counts (WBC ≥ 3 × 10^9/L, platelets ≥ 100 × 10^9/L). Obtain updated cardiac echo (baseline EF ≥ 50%). |
| **Vaccinations** | Administer pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) now; plan seasonal influenza vaccination; defer live vaccines until immune competence improves. |
| **Supportive Care** | Continue calcium supplementation (500 mg elemental Ca twice daily) and vitamin D3 (2000 IU daily). Encourage adequate protein intake and resistance exercise to preserve bone health. |
| **Follow‑up Appointment** | Return in 4 weeks for interim labs and symptom check; sooner if new pain, fevers, or bleeding occurs. |
| **Patient Education** | Reviewed signs of CRS (fever, hypotension, hypoxia) and instructed to call immediately if observed. Reinforced importance of adherence to appointment schedule and reporting any worsening neuropathic sensations. |

y.event_history:
The patient is a 59‑year‑old female named Anna Schmidt.
At age 57, the patient was diagnosed with stage III (ISS) MULTIPLE MYELOMA, MALIGNANT PLASMA CELL PROLIFERATION, IgA KAPPA type; serum M‑protein 1.2 g/dL, urine M‑protein 400 mg/24 h, involved free light chain 250 mg/L (κ/λ ratio 0.2), bone marrow plasma cells 48%; disease burden meets measurable criteria.
At age 57, bone‑marrow core biopsy demonstrated CD138+, CD56+, CD20‑ plasma cells with κ light‑chain restriction and 48 % clonal infiltration.
At age 57, whole‑body PET‑CT showed lytic lesions in the skull, pelvis, and a 1.5 cm extramedullary soft‑tissue deposit in the left posterior thigh; cancer present, neither responding nor progressing.
At age 57, oncologist noted active disease with CRAB features (hypercalcemia 11.4 mg/dL); disease status: active.
At age 57, first‑line regimen started with bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (VRd).
At age 58, after 6 cycles, serum M‑protein decreased to 0.6 g/dL, calcium normalized; very good partial response.
At age 58, patient experienced grade 3 thrombocytopenia (platelets 45 × 10⁹/L) persisting beyond treatment cycle, classified as residual toxicity > grade 1.
At age 58, due to platelet count, therapy was held and supportive transfusions given.
At age 58, second‑line therapy initiated with daratumumab + bortezomib + dexamethasone (DVd) to overcome refractory disease.
At age 59, after 2 months, serum M‑protein further declined to 0.3 g/dL; partial response.
At age 59, patient was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection (RNA positive) during routine screening; infection considered active and required antiviral therapy.
At age 60, oncologist documented active hepatitis C as a contraindication for enrollment in many clinical trials despite meeting disease and prior‑therapy criteria.
At age 60, third‑line regimen started with pomalidomide + dexamethasone (IMiD‑based) after holding anti‑CD38 due to infection concerns.
At age 61, serum M‑protein rose to 0.5 g/dL, indicating disease progression.
At age 61, patient experienced grade 2 peripheral neuropathy from prior proteasome inhibitor exposure.
At age 61, MRI pelvis showed new lytic lesion in the right iliac crest; cancer progressing.
At age 61, NGS of bone‑marrow specimen revealed KRAS p.G12D, NRAS p.Q61H, TP53 p.R175H, DIS3 p.E291K, 1q21 amplification, del(13q14), and a t(14;16)(q32;q23) IGH‑MAF translocation.
At age 62, oncologist noted that while the patient fulfills triple‑class exposure (PI, IMiD, anti‑CD38) and measurable disease, the presence of active hepatitis C infection and prior grade 3 thrombocytopenia (residual toxicity > grade 1) render her ineligible for the target trial.
At age 62, patient started direct‑acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C; tolerated well.
At age 63, after antiviral clearance, serum M‑protein stabilized at 0.45 g/dL; disease stable.
At age 63, repeat PET‑CT showed metabolic activity unchanged in known lesions.
At age 63, patient received a clinical‑trial bispecific antibody targeting BCMA (experimental) after resolution of hepatitis C.
At age 63, experienced grade 1 infusion‑related reaction, resolved with antihistamine premedication.
At age 64, disease remains measurable; patient now platelet counts recovered above 150 × 10⁹/L, but remains under close monitoring for trial eligibility.
